items.descriptionAdvanced: The Harar Jugol walls, a UNESCO World Heritage site, represent the historic fortification surrounding the ancient walled city of Harar. Constructed between the 13th and 16th centuries, these walls enclose 82 mosques, including the 10th-century Mosque of the Companions, and over 100 shrines. Harar is considered the fourth holiest city of Islam and features a unique architectural blend of traditional African and Islamic styles. The walls have served as a symbol of the city's independence and cultural identity for centuries. History K8 — Walled cities and Islamic architecture.
